newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Widow says Hebron deal vindicates Rabin's path.
newsitem.headline: Widow says Hebron deal vindicates Rabin's path.

text.p: Yitzhak Rabin's widow said on Wednesday an Israeli-PLO peace deal on Hebron had vindicated the slain Israeli prime minister's path and proved his assassination was in vain.

"If my emotions are charged today it is on the one hand a great sadness for an unnecessary victim on the altar of peace and on the other hand the satisfaction that his road and what he wanted to achieve is the winner," Leah Rabin told Israel Television's Channel One.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sealed a deal on Wednesday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to launch PLO self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron and to redeploy Israeli troops in West Bank rural areas.
The deal committed the right-wing Israeli leader to the interim Oslo peace deals former prime minister Rabin and his centre-left government signed with Arafat.
Rabin was assassinated in November 1995 by a right-wing religious Jew who opposed ceding occupied West Bank lands he believed God had promised the Jewish people.
Netanyahu defeated Rabin's successor Shimon Peres in May elections on a platform opposed to exchanging Israeli-occupied lands for peace.
But Leah Rabin said: "He (Rabin) is the winner and we're all following in his footsteps, including Mr Netanyahu's government and he himself."
